page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.cm4.2xlarge is an x86_64 architecture instance powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon E5-2667 v4 processor running at 3.2 GHz. It features 8 vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, providing 2 threads per core. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, resulting in a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It operates on the KVM hypervisor, does not include local storage, and lacks GPU accelerators. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate a mixed performance profile. The instance demonstrates average capabilities in memory bandwidth read-only tests, static web serving throughput, and single-threaded compression tasks such as gzip and bzip3. However, compute-intensive workloads show limitations, with stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU performance, Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression all falling into the bottom 25% tier. Cryptographic and database operations also register weak performance, as evidenced by low passmark CPU encryption and database operation scores.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.cm4.2xlarge offers a balanced resource density for general-purpose workloads that do not require high-performance computing or local storage. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent performance, but the older Intel Xeon E5-2667 v4 architecture presents a tradeoff in raw processing power and modern instruction sets, such as the lack of AVX-512 support. This instance is best suited for moderate general-purpose workloads, basic web serving, light text processing, and small-scale software compilation, while it is poorly suited for intensive database operations or large language model inference.
